The Flaw in Conventional Teas: Purity, Toxins, and Potency

When most people stroll down the grocery store aisle and pick up a box of standard tea bags, they assume they are making a healthy choice. Unfortunately, conventional agriculture and mass-market processing methods often compromise the very benefits that make tea so appealing in the first place.

  • Pesticide and Heavy Metal Contamination: Traditional tea leaves are frequently grown using synthetic pesticides, herbicides, and fertilizers. Furthermore, because tea plants act as hyper-accumulators from the soil, poor agricultural conditions can lead to heavy metal absorption.
  • Plastic Leaching in Teabags: Many commercial “silky” or pyramid tea bags are actually made of plastic (nylon or PET), which can leach microscopic plastic particles into your hot water during steeping.
  • Degraded Active Compounds: Standard manufacturing processes expose delicate antioxidants, polyphenols, and active compounds to heat, light, and air for months before they ever reach your mug, dramatically reducing their biological efficacy.

To truly experience the health-boosting properties of botanicals, you need a standard of purity and concentration that goes far beyond the supermarket shelf.
